title: "6. Cohort"

This script selects the published cohort, records how many patients each exclusion removes, and builds one row per patient with the values at the start of ART. It produces `cohort_days`, `patients` and `cohort_flow` for [7. Propensity score](07_propensity.qmd) and [8. Outcomes](08_outcomes.qmd).

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/06_cohort.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/R/06_cohort.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/R/functions.R)

Translated from the first part of [`stata/Do Final Analysis.do`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/stata/Do%20Final%20Analysis.do) (to line 57).

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/06_cohort.R")
source("_stata_links.R")
```

## Start at the first regimen

Days before the first regimen are dropped. Each patient's initial regimen, and whether it was twice daily, is that of regimen 1. Stata generated the value on regimen-1 days and used `carryforward` to copy it down; taking it from regimen 1 directly gives the same value on every row.

```{r}
#| label: start-at-first-regimen
#| eval: false
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| output: asis
stata_for("start-at-first-regimen")
```

## Exclusions

In the order Final Analysis.do applies them, with the number of patients left after each, which is what a STROBE flow diagram reports.

One Stata habit needs care. `drop if InitialRegimenBID` drops rows where the variable is non-zero, and Stata treats a missing value as non-zero, so patients with a missing value are dropped too. A patient whose first regimen started before 2008 has no regimen-1 rows on the grid, so their value is missing and they leave here. This is how the code enforces the start of enrollment. It sets no upper limit on the start date; the 2008-2011 enrollment window is assumed to come from the data extract ([details](study_methods.qmd#who-is-included)). Likewise `drop if prevcareelsewhere` drops patients with that field missing. The R filters keep only an explicit "no" (`%in% FALSE`, `%in% 0`) to match.

**From the code:** the exclusions for prior care elsewhere and missing insurance are not mentioned in the paper's methods; the code is the record of what was done.

```{r}
#| label: apply-exclusions
#| eval: false
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| output: asis
stata_for("apply-exclusions")
```

## Exposure and time

The STR group is patients whose initial regimen is a single tablet; among the three compared regimens that is Atripla. Time zero is the first day of regimen 1. `quarter` is 0 for day 0, then 1 to 4 for days 1-91, 92-182, 183-273 and 274-364, and missing afterwards (Stata: `egen Quarter = cut(DaysSinceARTInitiation), at(0,1,92,183,274,365) icodes`). `first_year` marks days 0-364.

```{r}
#| label: define-exposure-and-time
#| eval: false
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| output: asis
stata_for("define-exposure-and-time")
```

## One row per patient

Stata kept the daily data and picked out each patient's first day with `if FirstObservationOfSubject` on every command. R keeps a separate patient table, which is easier to read and to model. The baseline viral load and CD4 are the last values on or before the day ART started, with no limit on how long before.

```{r}
#| label: build-patient-table
#| eval: false
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| output: asis
stata_for("build-patient-table")
```

## Categories for the propensity model

Age, baseline viral load and baseline CD4 are put in the same groups as the Stata `egen cut()` lines. The insurance term in the propensity model, `i3.Insurance`, is an indicator for the third category in alphabetical order, because `encode` numbers text categories alphabetically. The paper describes this covariate as insured vs uninsured; which category is third depends on the categories in the real file.

```{r}
#| label: categorise-baseline-values
#| eval: false
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| output: asis
stata_for("categorise-baseline-values")
```
